headline: Learned models of proteins, nucleic acids, and molecules target design and prediction…
label: Deep Learning For Molecular Biology
summary: Recent preprints and publications pair generative and pretrained language models with biomolecular design and prediction tasks.
synthesis: The dominant thread is learned generative and representation models applied to biomolecular sequence, structure, and interaction problems. Generative approaches appear in regulatory DNA design, where LOCOGEN guides frozen diffusion models with a learned motif mask, in peptide structure prediction, where Neopep fine-tunes a sequence-conditioned diffusion model with reinforcement learning on machine-learned force field energies, and in drug design, where a latent quantum Wasserstein GAN is benchmarked on MOSES against classical latent GANs. Language-model representations drive other items: protein language model augmentation with ESM-3 generated data on small protein-complex sets, and PRIDA's protein-RNA interaction prediction using conditional domain-adversarial learning. PDI-Spot applies residue embeddings to protein-DNA hotspot identification. The set is heterogeneous, so the shared emphasis is learning under limited or transferred data rather than a single architecture. The newer element is explicit coupling of generative models to physics-based or motif-based constraints.
